plan: Store the constructor's dict as a private deep copy so external mutation of the input can never affect the workspace, and have to_data() return a fresh deep copy on every call.
Implement one recursive generator _walk(items, depth) that yields (item, depth) for every item in document order, recursing into 'section' and 'group' items; drive all three read operations from it.

total_word_count(): for notes, delete [[?identifier]] marker tokens (replacing with a space so adjacent words stay separate), then count maximal \b\w+\b runs; for references, add the declared word_count.
unresolved_markers(): collect marker identifiers from note text via the marker regex plus each reference's 'unresolved' list into a set, then return sorted(set) for unique lexicographic order.
outline(): first line is the workspace title, then for each walked item emit '  ' * depth + '<kind>: <title>' with top-level items at depth 1, joined with newlines for deterministic output.

move(): validate everything before mutating — string-typed ids, item lookup, destination lookup ('workspace' literal or a section/group id), non-container destination rejection, self/descendant containment rejection, and integer index within 0..post-removal destination length — then pop the item from its parent list and append or insert it. Because no mutation precedes the last check, any ValueError leaves to_data() exactly unchanged, and a successful move relocates the intact subtree.
mechanisms: deep-copy isolation at construction and export
single recursive document-order walker shared by all summaries
marker-stripping-then-word-regex counting for notes; declared word_count for references
set-union plus lexicographic sort for unresolved marker identifiers
depth-indexed indentation rendering for the outline
validate-before-mutate move with containment (no-cycle) and post-removal index-bound checks
